discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.

Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

- edge-opportunity-end: create-opportunity.success -> complete.input
- edge-nurture-end: add-to-nurture.success -> complete.input

- The happy path: New lead -> Enrich -> (if qualified) Create CRM opportunity -> Complete.

- manual-review exists on the canvas but has no connections.
- No failure/error edges are connected (e.g., enrich-company.failure is not wired).

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

- edge-nurture-end — add-to-nurture.success → complete.input

discover_workflow

edit_workflow

undo_workflow_edit

Here’s what’s on the canvas now.

Summary
- 7 nodes (start → actions/condition → end) and 6 edges connecting them.

Nodes
- new-lead — Start node — label: "New lead submitted" — position: (40, 220). Outgoing port: next
- enrich-company — Action — label: "Enrich company" — position: (280, 220). Property: system. Ports: input, success
- qualified-lead — Condition — label: "Qualified lead?" — position: (520, 220). Property: minimumScore. Ports: input, yes, no
- create-opportunity — Action — label: "Create CRM opportunity" — position: (760, 100). Property: destination. Ports: input, success
- add-to-nurture — Action — label: "Add to nurture campaign" — position: (760, 300). Property: destination. Ports: input, success
- manual-review — Action — label: "Manual review" — position: (760, 500). Property: queue = "Sales operations". (Currently has no connections.)
- complete — End — label: "Complete" — position: (1020, 220). Input port

Edges (by id)
- edge-lead-enrich: new-lead (next) → enrich-company (input)
- edge-enrich-qualified: enrich-company (success) → qualified-lead (input)
- edge-qualified-opportunity (label "Qualified"): qualified-lead (yes) → create-opportunity (input)
- edge-qualified-nurture (label "Nurture"): qualified-lead (no) → add-to-nurture (input)
- edge-opportunity-end: create-opportunity (success) → complete (input)
- edge-nurture-end: add-to-nurture (success) → complete (input)

Notes
- The workflow starts at "New lead submitted", flows through company enrichment and qualification, then either creates a CRM opportunity or adds the lead to a nurture campaign, both paths ending at "Complete".
- "Manual review" is present on the canvas but is not connected to the flow.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Thoughts:
I inspected the workflow. Summary: there are 7 nodes and 6 edges on the canvas. Below are the items and how they’re connected.

Nodes
- new-lead — Start node (id: new-lead)
  - Label: "New lead submitted"
  - Position: (40, 220)
  - Property names: ["source"]

- enrich-company — Action node (id: enrich-company)
  - Label: "Enrich company"
  - Position: (280, 220)
  - Property names: ["system"]

- qualified-lead — Condition node (id: qualified-lead)
  - Label: "Qualified lead?"
  - Position: (520, 220)
  - Property names: ["minimumScore"]

- create-opportunity — Action node (id: create-opportunity)
  - Label: "Create CRM opportunity"
  - (Position not explicitly listed in the inspected pages, but it is on the right of qualified-lead)

- add-to-nurture — Action node (id: add-to-nurture)
  - Label: "Add to nurture campaign"
  - (Position not explicitly listed in the inspected pages, but it is to the lower-right of qualified-lead)

- manual-review — Action node (id: manual-review)
  - Label: "Manual review"
  - Position: (760, 500)
  - Property names: ["queue"]
  - Note: this node currently has no connections (it’s isolated)

- complete — End node (id: complete)
  - Label: "Complete"
  - Position: (1020, 220)
  - No properties

Edges (6)
- edge-lead-enrich
  - new-lead.next -> enrich-company.input

- edge-enrich-qualified
  - enrich-company.success -> qualified-lead.input

- edge-qualified-opportunity (label: "Qualified")
  - qualified-lead.yes -> create-opportunity.input

- edge-qualified-nurture
  - qualified-lead.no -> add-to-nurture.input

- edge-opportunity-end
  - create-opportunity.input? -> complete.input
  - (create-opportunity -> complete incoming edge id: edge-opportunity-end)

- edge-nurture-end
  - add-to-nurture -> complete.input (edge id: edge-nurture-end)

Notes
- The main linear flow: New lead submitted -> Enrich company -> Qualified lead? branch.
  - If yes: Create CRM opportunity -> Complete.
  - If no: Add to nurture campaign -> Complete.
- The "Manual review" node exists but is not connected to the rest of the flow.
- Total counts reported: 7 nodes, 6 edges.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.

discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, and again after conflicts. Returns a compact page of item IDs, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. Follow nextCursor for more IDs.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow to inspect up to five current nodes or connections by stable application ID, including properties and relationships.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Set baseRevision to its exact revision, or Number(surface.documentVersion) for a SurfaceSnapshot. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Atomically applies up to 20 commands; updateNode patch.label accepts a string or a copied Snapshot label object. On conflict, follow recovery.
show_workflow_item
Use a current item ID from discover_workflow to select a workflow node or connection and bring it into view. For nodes, also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Focus one named page target on the next browser focus or accessibility interaction. Pass exactly one targetId value returned by discover_workflow.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes and validation problems for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use this as the final proof step after edit_workflow. Pass its operationId to bring that history entry into view and move keyboard focus to it as visible evidence for the user.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.
